diagnosis.summary: Telegram sendMessage returned 429 with retry_after 30 indicating a provider rate limit rejection.
alternate_explanations: Transient network error before rate limit header processing.

proposal.summary: Escalate provider rate limit rejection to engineering investigation.
reasons: Provider rate limits and outages belong to engineering/provider investigation.

diagnosis.summary: The delivery attempt to Telegram failed with 'Connection refused before request transmission', indicating a transport or provider availability failure before request transmission.
alternate_explanations: Provider outage or firewall blocking outbound connections to Telegram API endpoint.

proposal.summary: Escalate provider connectivity failure for engineering and provider investigation.
reasons: Connection was refused before request transmission, pointing to infrastructure or transport failure rather than customer configuration fault.
preconditions: Confirm provider network stability and outbound connectivity.

diagnosis.summary: Configured Telegram token is absent resulting in delivery failure.
alternate_explanations: Worker environment credential fallback might be misconfigured.

proposal.summary: Request manual operator action to supply the missing Telegram token configuration.
reasons: The configured Telegram token is absent.
Customer-controlled configuration repair is required for missing credentials.
preconditions: Verify that the Telegram bot token is configured correctly in the customer-controlled settings.

diagnosis.summary: Telegram action rejected due to an invalid channel username, indicating a customer configuration fault in the destination/recipient field.
alternate_explanations: Temporary platform routing glitch causing destination parse failure.

proposal.summary: Review and correct the Telegram channel username or destination configuration before any future retry attempts.
reasons: The provider explicitly rejected the request with 'Invalid channel username', which points to a customer-controlled configuration issue in the destination settings.
preconditions: Customer updates the invalid channel username configuration.

diagnosis.summary: Telegram action failed because the resolved destination is empty due to a missing template path.
alternate_explanations: Worker environment fallback could have affected path resolution.
Bot membership or permission issues could have contributed to send failure.

proposal.summary: Request manual operator intervention to configure the missing template path and correct the empty destination.
reasons: Observed facts establish a template path missing error and resolved destination empty fault.
Customer-controlled configuration of destination and template path requires manual fix.
preconditions: Confirm bot membership and permissions outside the agent.
Verify template paths and ensure destination is correctly provided.

diagnosis.summary: Provider rejected the destination due to an invalid destination format for the telegram action.
alternate_explanations: Destination might be missing required parameters or recipient formatting.

proposal.summary: Review and correct the recipient destination configuration for the telegram action to resolve the invalid destination format rejection.
reasons: The provider rejected the destination with observed fact destination_format_invalid.
Customer-controlled destination configuration requires manual fix.
preconditions: Confirm correct destination formatting and recipient configuration outside the agent.

diagnosis.summary: Unsupported action type encountered, handler not registered.
alternate_explanations: Handler registration defect or missing action handler implementation.

proposal.summary: Escalate unsupported handler/action type defect to engineering.
reasons: Unsupported action type and unregistered handler belong to engineering/provider investigation.
Never ask the customer to register a platform handler or repair provider infrastructure.
preconditions: Engineering review of handler registry and unsupported action types.

diagnosis.summary: Execution failed due to missing action handler (No action handler found), indicating a handler registry or version defect.
alternate_explanations: The action type may have been removed or never registered in the handler registry.

proposal.summary: Escalate to engineering to investigate the missing action handler and platform registry configuration.
reasons: Handler registration and version defects belong to engineering and provider investigation.
The error explicitly states 'No action handler found'.
preconditions: Engineering review of the handler registry and deployment version.

diagnosis.summary: Provider response was lost after request transmission, leaving delivery outcome unknown.
alternate_explanations: The message may have been successfully delivered despite the missing response.
The request may have been dropped or rejected upstream without reaching the final provider endpoint.

proposal.summary: Abstain from replay or definitive delivery claims due to unknown provider delivery outcome and missing evidence.
reasons: Delivery outcome is unknown following transmission failure.
Required evidence items are completely unavailable.
Runbook rules mandate treating missing receipts and unknown outcomes as abstained.

diagnosis.summary: Duplicate exhausted-failure record detected with identical retry identity seen twice, indicating a duplicate or stale finding.
alternate_explanations: Broker retry duplication without new authority or effect.

proposal.summary: No action required for duplicate or stale findings or repeated investigations.
reasons: The failure context indicates a duplicate exhausted-failure record with the same retry identity seen twice.
Broker duplication does not create new authority.

diagnosis.summary: The failure context indicates a republished event for a stage already marked SUCCESS (stale event received), which falls under duplicate or stale findings.

proposal.summary: No action is required as the event represents a duplicate or stale finding for a stage that has already succeeded.
reasons: The stage is already successful and a stale event was received.
Never reset SUCCESS or republish a raw event per runbook guidance.

diagnosis.summary: Database sink encountered a Kafka dead-letter publication failure with unknown delivery outcome and missing evidence.
alternate_explanations: The failure might stem from transient messaging infrastructure outages.
Downstream sink misconfiguration could prevent dead-letter routing.

proposal.summary: Delivery outcome is unknown and required evidence is missing, requiring escalation.
reasons: Delivery outcome is unknown and evidence is incomplete.
Required missing evidence prevents deterministic replay or safe owner configuration fixes.
preconditions: Obtain complete execution records and broker receipts before determining final action.

diagnosis.summary: An email SDK error value was discarded and success status was recorded, but delivery outcome remains unknown and required evidence is missing.
alternate_explanations: The email transmission may have failed completely without reaching the provider.
The message may have been successfully delivered despite the discarded SDK error.

proposal.summary: Escalate due to unknown delivery outcome and missing evidence.
reasons: Delivery outcome is unknown and conflicting or missing delivery evidence prevents a definitive conclusion.
preconditions: Obtain complete SDK results and provider receipts.

diagnosis.summary: Investigation abstained because delivery outcome is unknown and multiple crucial items of evidence are unavailable.
alternate_explanations: The provider encountered an unknown failure state.
Inputs or handlers were improperly configured.

proposal.summary: Escalate for investigation due to unknown delivery outcome and missing evidence.
reasons: Delivery outcome is unknown and contradictory or insufficient evidence prevents a definitive fault diagnosis.
Required evidence items are completely unavailable.
preconditions: Obtain complete provider delivery receipts and execution records before any further evaluation.

diagnosis.summary: Delivery outcome is unknown and required evidence is missing, preventing a definitive bounded diagnosis.
alternate_explanations: Provider credentials may be invalid or rejected.
Execution evidence is incomplete or simulated.

proposal.summary: Escalate for investigation due to unknown delivery outcome and missing evidence.
reasons: Delivery outcome is unknown and contradictory evidence is absent, requiring abstention per routing rules.
preconditions: Complete evidence must be gathered before any future consideration.

diagnosis.summary: Provider result is unavailable after the deduplication window expired, and delivery outcome remains unknown.
alternate_explanations: Provider may have successfully processed the request prior to window expiration without returning a receipt.

proposal.summary: Abstain from replay or modification due to unknown delivery outcome and expired deduplication window.
reasons: Delivery outcome is unknown and the deduplication window has expired.
Replay is unsafe when provider delivery is unverified and deduplication guarantees are no longer active.
preconditions: Preserve all evidence and reconcile with the provider.

limitations: Small samples: 18 development / 8 held-out cases; targets are descriptive, not statistical release evidence.
Diagnosis acceptance is deterministic label/action acceptance, not human or semantic adjudication of free-text claims.

Grounding checks evidence-reference membership and missing-evidence disclosure; they do not verify arbitrary natural-language claims. Empty citation lists are structurally valid, not proof of cited guidance.
Retrieval is measured against captured controlled-fixture graph queries and returned context, separately from Phase 11 fixture-query recall; live retrieval quality is unmeasured.
Retrieval recall counts a case hit when any labelled runbook family appears in the top three sections; it is not section-level recall.
Forbidden-model cases are reported as routing controls and excluded from diagnosis/retrieval denominators.
Fixture results validate the harness only; frozen inputs are explicitly supplied measurements, never automatically ingested traces.
Frozen re-evaluation is offline. Original capture may call the selected diagnosis model only; no action providers, replay or approval mutations are permitted.
Unknown cost/usage/latency stays null. Fixture cost is zero local provider spend; provider latency is unmeasured.
Live replay remains disabled; approval is authority only. Provider non-delivery semantics remain unproven.

Phase 2 cases lack complete live replay facts. Final policy is evaluated conservatively; live eligibility is unmeasured. Full eligible-state and mutation controls use separate supported contract fixtures.

limitations: Small samples: 18 development / 8 held-out cases; targets are descriptive, not statistical release evidence.
Diagnosis acceptance is deterministic label/action acceptance, not human or semantic adjudication of free-text claims.

Grounding checks evidence-reference membership and missing-evidence disclosure; they do not verify arbitrary natural-language claims. Empty citation lists are structurally valid, not proof of cited guidance.
Retrieval is measured against captured controlled-fixture graph queries and returned context, separately from Phase 11 fixture-query recall; live retrieval quality is unmeasured.
Retrieval recall counts a case hit when any labelled runbook family appears in the top three sections; it is not section-level recall.
Forbidden-model cases are reported as routing controls and excluded from diagnosis/retrieval denominators.
Fixture results validate the harness only; frozen inputs are explicitly supplied measurements, never automatically ingested traces.
Frozen re-evaluation is offline. Original capture may call the selected diagnosis model only; no action providers, replay or approval mutations are permitted.
Unknown cost/usage/latency stays null. Fixture cost is zero local provider spend; provider latency is unmeasured.
Live replay remains disabled; approval is authority only. Provider non-delivery semantics remain unproven.

Phase 2 cases lack complete live replay facts. Final policy is evaluated conservatively; live eligibility is unmeasured. Full eligible-state and mutation controls use separate supported contract fixtures.
